task.description: Independently re-verify REQ-039 (Sandbox pool and fixture loader) is genuinely done before DOC-UPDATER flips its status. Do not trust TEST-RUNNER's report alone -- re-run the suite yourself.
acceptance_criteria: Each of REQ-039's 6 acceptance criteria checked explicitly against the actual code/test, not against any prior agent's summary

result.summary: Independent re-verification, branch feature/WF02-REQ039-20260817 (commit 5a4a5a7). (1) mix test run fresh twice myself: unpinned seed -> 'Result: 323 passed (4 properties, 319 tests)', exit 0; second run with --seed 12345 -> identical '323 passed (4 properties, 319 tests)', exit 0. Matches TEST-RUNNER's step-04 report exactly, independently reproduced rather than trusted. Also queried Postgres directly after both runs (mix run -e against pg_catalog.pg_namespace for 'sandbox_%') and found zero orphaned sandbox schemas -- cleanup is real, not just claimed. (2) Read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-039 entry (lines 1822-1873) and checked each of its 6 acceptance_criteria directly against the shipped code/tests myself: AC1 (empty-pool immediate claim, real schema) -- confirmed in sandbox_pool.ex's handle_provision_now/provision_sandbox (CREATE SCHEMA, no IF NOT EXISTS) and sandbox_pool_test.exs's 'empty pool' describe block, which asserts against information_schema.schemata directly (not just the return value). AC2 (blocking on exhausted quota, timeout -> :sandbox_unavailable) -- confirmed in handle_queue_or_reject/Process.send_after/handle_info({:claim_timeout,...}) and the 3 tests covering release-driven hand-off, real-timeout path, and max_wait_ms<=0 immediate-reject. AC3 (release drops schema for real, frees slot) -- confirmed in handle_call({:release,...})/drop_schema/service_next_waiter and the test asserting schema_exists? is false post-release plus a subsequent claim succeeds. AC4 (allowlist rejection before any SQL) -- confirmed in FixtureLoader.load_fixtures_only/3's with-chain (validate_schema_name, then validate_table_names, both complete before apply_fixtures/3 is ever called) and the test proving zero rows land even for an allowlisted table when batched with a non-allowlisted one. AC5 (TRUNCATE-before-insert idempotent retry) -- confirmed in apply_fixtures/3 (TRUNCATE each distinct table inside the same transaction, then INSERT) and the 3 fixture_loader_test.exs tests (identical retry, changed retry replaces, empty-list no-op). AC6 (moduledoc names the process-per-instance-vs-row open question, left for CODE-DESIGNER) -- read sandbox_pool.ex lines 13-30 directly: the moduledoc has an explicit '## Process-per-instance vs. row-based state (REQ-039's open question, resolved here)' section that names stage-2-event-store-definitions.md's 'Early findings' section by name (verified that section header exists at stage-2-event-store-definitions.md:20) and states CODE-DESIGNER resolved it in the design doc -- matches AC6's text exactly. All 6 confirmed by direct inspection of the actual shipped .ex/.exs files, not by re-reading CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's or TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's summaries (though my independent reading agrees with both). (3) Staleness check: docs/requirements.yaml REQ-039 status is still 'in_progress' as expected (DOC-UPDATER, Step 6, hasn't run) -- not staleness. docs/status/requirement_status.yaml has exactly one REQ-039 entry (line 2610, event: started, 2026-08-17T08:03:14Z) and no 'done' event yet -- consistent, not stale. REQ-039's own text explicitly leaves the process-vs-row choice open for CODE-DESIGNER 'at WF-02 design time' rather than asserting an answer, so the shipped GenServer-singleton design is a resolution of an explicitly-deferred question, not a drift from the requirement text. Checked REQ-039's depends_on: [REQ-022] is genuinely status: done in docs/requirements.yaml (line 845). Checked git diff main...HEAD --stat: 19 files changed, scope is exactly config wiring (dev/prod/test.exs), lib/letflow/application.ex supervision wiring, the two new lib/ modules, the two new test files, the design doc, the test spec, handoff files, and the test report -- no stray or out-of-scope files. (4) Sanity-checked the gate sequence is real, not just claimed: step-01b (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR), step-02c (SECURITY-REVIEWER), step-02d (REVIEWER), step-03b (TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR), step-04 (TEST-RUNNER) all show status: COMPLETED and result.status: PASS, each with substantive independent-verification summaries (not rubber-stamps) -- read all 5 in full. REQ-039 is genuinely done.
